if (!file.exists("met_all.gz"))
  download.file(
    url = "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/USCbiostats/data-science-data/master/02_met/met_all.gz",
    destfile = "met_all.gz",
    method   = "libcurl",
    timeout  = 60
  )
met <- read.csv("met_all.gz")
met <- met[met$temp > -17, ]
met$temp[met$temp==9999.0] <- NA
met$date <- as.Date(
  paste(met$year, met$month, met$day, sep = "-")
)
met <- met[met$day <= 7, ]
library(dplyr)

Attaching package: 'dplyr'
The following objects are masked from 'package:stats':

    filter, lag
The following objects are masked from 'package:base':

    intersect, setdiff, setequal, union
met_weekly <- summarize(met,
                       temp = mean(temp),
                       rh = mean(rh),
                       wind.sp = mean(wind.sp),
                       vis.dist = mean(vis.dist),
                       lat = mean(lat),
                       lon = mean(lon),
                       elev = mean(elev),
                       dew.point = mean(dew.point),
                       .by = USAFID)
met_weekly$region <- ifelse(
  met_weekly$lat >= 39.71 & met_weekly$lon < -98, "NW",
  ifelse(
    met_weekly$lat < 39.71 & met_weekly$lon < -98, "SW",
    ifelse(
      met_weekly$lat >= 39.71 & met_weekly$lon >= -98, "NE",
      "SE"
    )
  )
)
table(met_weekly$region)

 NE  NW  SE  SW 
484 147 653 296 
library(ggplot2)

ggplot(met_weekly, aes(x = 1, y = rh)) +
  geom_violin(na.rm = TRUE) +
  facet_wrap(~ region) +
  labs(
    title = "Relative Humidity by Region",
    x = "Direction",
    y = "Relative Humidity"
  )
Warning in min(x): no non-missing arguments to min; returning Inf
Warning in max(x): no non-missing arguments to max; returning -Inf

there are 4 different graphs reflecting latitude and longtitude reflecting different shapes within the direction

ggplot(met_weekly, aes(x = dew.point, y = rh, color = region)) +
  geom_point(na.rm = TRUE) +
  stat_smooth(method = "lm", na.rm = TRUE)
`geom_smooth()` using formula = 'y ~ x'
met_weekly$elev.category <- cut(
  met_weekly$elev,
  breaks = c(-Inf, 500, 1000, Inf),
  labels = c("Low", "Medium", "High")
)

ggplot(
  met_weekly[!is.na(met_weekly$elev.category) &
               !is.na(met_weekly$region), ],
  aes(x = elev.category, fill = region)
) +
  geom_bar(position = "dodge") +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set2") +
  labs(
    title = "Weather Stations by Elevation and Region",
    x = "Elevation Category",
    y = "Number of Weather Stations",
    fill = "Region"
  )

In the graph we can see that there are significant number of SE weather stations but they contain low levels of elevation. We also see that SW and NW has multiple weather stations in all different elevation regions

ggplot(met_weekly, aes(x = region, y = dew.point)) +
  stat_summary(
    fun.data = "mean_sdl",
    geom = "point",
    na.rm = TRUE
  ) +
  stat_summary(
    fun.data = "mean_sdl",
    geom = "errorbar",
    na.rm = TRUE
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Mean Dew Point by Region",
    x = "Region",
    y = "Mean Dew Point"
  )

Dew Point contains the highest mean and maximum values in the SE region. The region with the most variability is the NW region as the maximum and minimum values contain mean dew points from 1 - 22.5.

ggplot(met_weekly, aes(x = region, y = wind.sp)) +
  stat_summary(
    fun.data = "mean_sdl",
    geom = "point",
    na.rm = TRUE
  ) +
  stat_summary(
    fun.data = "mean_sdl",
    geom = "errorbar",
    na.rm = TRUE
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Mean Wind Speed by Region",
    x = "Region",
    y = "Mean Wind Speed"
  )

Mean Wind Speed by Region contains lots of Variability is all Regions. The Maximum and Minimum Wind Speeds are highly dispersed from the mean.

library("maps")
library(ggplot2)

met_map <- na.omit(met_weekly[, c("rh", "lat", "lon")])

ggplot(met_map, aes(lon, lat)) +
  annotation_borders("state") +
  geom_point(aes(color = rh)) +
  geom_point(
    data = met_map[rank(-met_map$rh) <= 10, ],
    size = 4,
    shape = 1
  ) +
  scale_color_gradient(
    low = "yellow",
    high = "darkblue",
    name = "Relative Humidity"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Relative Humidity Across the US",
    x = "Longitude",
    y = "Latitude"
  )

As we look from West to East coast relative humidity increases the farther east and lower south we look at

library(ggplot2)
library(ggthemes)

ggplot(met_weekly, aes(dew.point, rh, color = region)) +
  geom_point(na.rm = TRUE) +
  theme_economist() +
  labs(
    title = "Dew Point and Relative Humidity",
    x = "Dew Point",
    y = "Relative Humidity",
    color = "Region"
  )
